subtype: Child learning what anger feels like [Actor]
passage: In the kindergarten block, Ojas and another boy grabbed the same toy truck. Ojas's cheeks went hot pink and his fists squeezed shut. Nirmala Miss knelt beside him. "Ojas, look, your hands are squeezed into balls. Your cheeks are warm. Can you feel your heart going fast?" Ojas nodded, fists still tight. "That's what angry feels like in your body. It's okay to feel it." They opened their fists slowly together, like flowers. Later, when a block tower fell, Ojas held up his fists. "Miss! Angry hands!"

qa.q: What did Ojas and the other boy both grab?
qa.a: They grabbed the same toy truck.

qa.q: What was Ojas feeling when his fists squeezed shut?
qa.a: Ojas was angry; his hot cheeks, tight fists and fast heart showed it.

qa.q: How did Nirmala Miss help Ojas understand anger?
qa.a: Nirmala Miss named the body signs aloud, the squeezed hands, warm cheeks and fast heart, then opened fists slowly with Ojas.

qa.q: What does Nirmala Miss probably think when Ojas shouts "Angry hands!"?
qa.a: Nirmala Miss is likely pleased, since Ojas is noticing the signs before an outburst, the start of self-control.

grounding: A young child feels hot cheeks, tight fists and a fast heart before an outburst, and an adult naming these signs lays the base for self-control.

subtype: Child learning what anger feels like [Actor]
passage: I'm Rashmi, and my brother Eshaan is five. Last night we played ludo, and when my token cut his, his face went red and his jaw locked. His hand went up to swipe the board. Mumma caught his hand softly. "Eshaan, your face is hot, and your hand wants to hit. Is your heart going fast?" He nodded, breathing hard. "That's anger coming. Let's squeeze the cushion instead." He squeezed it so hard his knuckles went white. I don't know what was going on inside him, but after a bit he said, "Heart slow now," and rolled the dice.

qa.q: What game were Rashmi and Eshaan playing?
qa.a: They played ludo.

qa.q: What do Eshaan's red face and locked jaw suggest?
qa.a: They suggest Eshaan was getting angry after his token was cut, though Rashmi could not be sure what was going on inside.

qa.q: What did Mumma do that could help Eshaan later on?
qa.a: Mumma named the signs, a hot face, a hand that wants to hit and a fast heart, and offered a cushion to squeeze, giving Eshaan a way to notice anger early.

qa.q: What might Rashmi have felt as Eshaan's hand went up to swipe the board?
qa.a: Rashmi may have felt worried the game would be ruined, then relieved when Eshaan rolled the dice again.

grounding: A young child's hot face, locked jaw and fast heart come before an outburst, and a parent helps him notice these signs.

subtype: Child learning what anger feels like [Actor]
passage: In the courtyard of their house outside Nashik, Gargi's cousin stepped on her clay elephant, and one leg snapped off. Gargi's cheeks went hot. Her fists squeezed shut. She lifted one fist high. Reena Kaki caught her eye from the well. 'Gargi, look at your hands. So tight!' Gargi looked down, surprised. 'Cheeks red like tomatoes. Heart going fast, na? That's angry.' Gargi's fist wobbled. 'I am angry!' 'Yes. Let's put the angry in the water.' They splashed cold water on Gargi's hands. The fists opened. Then they pressed the leg back on.

qa.q: What happened to Gargi's clay elephant?
qa.a: One leg snapped off.

qa.q: What was Gargi feeling when she lifted her fist?
qa.a: She was angry and upset that her clay elephant was broken.

qa.q: What did Reena Kaki do to help Gargi notice her anger?
qa.a: She named what she saw in Gargi's body, tight fists, red cheeks and a fast heart, and called it angry.

qa.q: How might the cousin have felt when Gargi raised her fist?
qa.a: The cousin may have felt scared or guilty about stepping on the elephant.

grounding: Shows a young child's hot cheeks, tight fists and fast heart before an outburst, and an adult naming these body signs to help her notice anger.

subtype: Child learning what anger feels like [Actor]
passage: In the Leicester flat, Bilal was one square away from winning snakes and ladders. Then Omar, his dad, rolled a six and climbed the long ladder to the top. 'I win!' Bilal's face went pink. His fingers curled into fists over the board, ready to sweep it off. Omar noticed. He put his hands up gently. 'Wait. Bilal, look at your fists. They've gone really tight. And your face is hot, isn't it?' Bilal stared at his hands. 'My heart's doing drums.' 'That's what angry feels like. Clever you for noticing.' Bilal breathed out hard through his nose, like a dragon. The fists loosened. 'Rematch?' he said.

qa.q: What did Omar roll to win?
qa.a: A six.

qa.q: What was Bilal feeling when his fingers curled into fists?
qa.a: He was angry and frustrated at losing when he was so close to winning.

qa.q: What could a parent learn from Omar's response?
qa.a: Point out the body signs calmly, like tight fists and a hot face, and name them as anger before the outburst.

qa.q: What would change if Omar had just said, 'Don't be a bad loser'?
qa.a: Bilal might have swept the board off and felt ashamed without learning what his body was telling him.

grounding: Shows a young child's tight fists, hot face and drumming heart before an outburst, and a parent helping him notice the signs as anger.

subtype: Child learning what anger feels like [Actor]
passage: At the kindergarten water tap, Karan pushed in front of Pradeep. Pradeep's face went red and his fists clenched. He opened his mouth to shout. Shreya Miss knelt beside him first. 'Pradeep, your hands have gone into hard fists. Is your face hot?' Pradeep nodded hard. 'And your heart? Put your hand here.' He felt it thumping. 'That's your angry feeling. It's okay to feel angry. Shall we tell Karan with words?' Pradeep took a big breath. 'Karan, I was first!' Karan stepped back. Later, Pradeep coloured the top of a paper anger thermometer red. 'That's my fists,' he said.

qa.q: Who pushed in front of Pradeep?
qa.a: Karan.

qa.q: What was Pradeep feeling when his fists clenched?
qa.a: He was angry that Karan had pushed in front of him.

qa.q: What did Shreya Miss do before Pradeep could shout?
qa.a: She knelt beside him and helped him notice his tight fists, hot face and thumping heart as his angry feeling.

qa.q: How might Karan see what happened at the tap?
qa.a: Karan may have felt surprised when Pradeep spoke up clearly, and realised the pushing in had been unfair.

grounding: Shows a young child noticing the tight fists, hot face and fast heart of anger with a teacher's words, laying the base for later self-control.

subtype: Child learning what anger feels like [Actor]
passage:
Monday: Keerthana's tower fell when her big brother Sumit bumped the table. Her cheeks went hot, her fists clenched, and she kicked the blocks everywhere. Amma knelt down. 'Your fists are all squeezed and your face is red. That's anger.'
Thursday: Sumit took the last dosa. Keerthana felt her heart go fast. She looked at her hands. 'Amma! My fists are squeezed!' Amma nodded. 'Good noticing. Let's squeeze the pillow.'
Next Sunday: When Sumit teased her drawing, Keerthana stamped her foot, then stopped. 'My cheeks are hot. I need the pillow.' She squeezed it hard, then told him, 'Don't tease. It makes me angry.'

qa.q: What did Keerthana squeeze?
qa.a: The pillow.

qa.q: How was Keerthana feeling when she kicked the blocks on Monday?
qa.a: She was angry and frustrated, with hot cheeks and clenched fists, but didn't yet know what the feeling was.

qa.q: How did Amma help Keerthana learn about anger?
qa.a: By naming the body signs, squeezed fists and a red face, as anger, and offering the pillow to squeeze.

qa.q: How might Sumit have felt when Keerthana told him not to tease?
qa.a: Sumit might have felt surprised, hearing his little sister name her anger instead of kicking.

grounding: Over a week a young child learns to notice hot cheeks and clenched fists before an outburst, laying the base for self-control.
